stem.en: "Poets and Pancakes" is taken from which book?

explanation.en: It is an extract from Asokamitran's memoir My Years with Boss.

stem.en: What was "Pancake"?

options.en: A snack served in the canteen
The brand name of a make-up material

explanation.en: Pancake was the brand of make-up material that Gemini Studios bought in large quantities.

stem.en: Who was "the Boss" of Gemini Studios?

explanation.en: S. S. Vasan founded and ran Gemini Studios and was called the Boss.

stem.en: What was the author's job at Gemini Studios?

options.en: Cutting out newspaper clippings and filing them

explanation.en: He cut out and filed newspaper clippings; others thought he was doing nothing.

stem.en: Why was the office boy frustrated?

options.en: He was going to be promoted
He had hoped to become a star or writer but ended up painting crowd players

explanation.en: His dreams of fame had come to nothing, and he spent his days making up crowd players.

stem.en: Whom did the office boy blame for his failure?

explanation.en: He directed his anger at Subbu, the number two at Gemini.

stem.en: Which of these was NOT one of Subbu's qualities?

options.en: He was loyal to the Boss
He was a gifted poet and actor
He was mean and unwelcoming to guests
He could suggest many ways to shoot a scene

explanation.en: Subbu was known for generosity and hospitality; his house was always full of people.

stem.en: What makes the description of the office boy ironic?

options.en: He was a middle-aged man still called a boy
He was the richest man in the studio

explanation.en: Calling a middle-aged man an office boy is a small irony that the author enjoys.

stem.en: Which group visited Madras and staged plays like Jotham Valley?

explanation.en: The Moral Re-Armament (MRA) group, which opposed communism, staged these plays.

stem.en: Why did the staff of Gemini Studios fail to understand the English poet?

options.en: He did not speak at all
They could not follow his accent

explanation.en: His accent was unfamiliar, so nobody understood what he was saying.

stem.en: Which book helped the author understand why the English poet had been invited?

explanation.en: The God That Failed contained Spender's essay on his disillusionment with communism.

stem.en: What linked Stephen Spender with the Boss of Gemini Studios?

explanation.en: Spender had broken with communism, and the Boss too was against it, which explains the invitation.

stem.en: The tone of "Poets and Pancakes" is best described as

explanation.en: The author writes with light, ironic humour, often laughing at himself.

stem.en: The author's remark that the make-up department showed national integration is an example of

explanation.en: He uses a grand phrase for a mixed team in a make-up room, with gentle irony.

stem.en: Which theme is shown through the office boy?

options.en: The gap between ambition and achievement

explanation.en: His unfulfilled dreams show the gap between ambition and what one actually achieves.

stem.en: What does the title "Poets and Pancakes" bring together?

options.en: The creative and the commercial sides of film-making

explanation.en: Poets stand for creative talent and pancake (make-up) for the business of making films.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Gemini Studios welcomed the Moral Re-Armament group.
Reason (R): The MRA was opposed to communism, and so was the Boss of Gemini.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both are true, and R explains A: the shared anti-communist outlook explains the welcome.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): The staff at Gemini Studios enjoyed and understood the English poet's speech.
Reason (R): Stephen Spender was the editor of The Encounter.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is false: no one understood his speech. R is true: Spender edited The Encounter.

stem.en: Which character in "Poets and Pancakes" is most like the junior artist in the passage?

options.en: The office boy in the make-up department

explanation.en: Like the office boy, the junior artist joined with creative dreams, paints extras and blames a senior.

passage.en: A film production house in the 1970s employed a team of thirty make-up artists from eight different states, who worked side by side in one long, brightly lit room. One junior artist, who had joined hoping to become a scriptwriter, spent most of his day painting the faces of crowd extras. He often grumbled that the head of the script team had blocked his chances. The company once hosted a visiting playwright from Europe whose speeches no one in the office could follow.

stem.en: The make-up team "from eight different states" reflects which idea in the chapter?

options.en: The author's ironic praise of national integration

explanation.en: A mixed-region make-up team is what the author jokingly calls national integration.

stem.en: Match: (i) S. S. Vasan (ii) Kothamangalam Subbu (iii) Stephen Spender (iv) the office boy

options.en: (i) English poet (ii) the Boss (iii) office boy (iv) the number two
(i) the number two (ii) English poet (iii) the Boss (iv) MRA leader
(i) the Boss (ii) the number two (iii) English poet (iv) frustrated would-be poet
(i) office boy (ii) frustrated poet (iii) the Boss (iv) English poet

explanation.en: Vasan was the Boss, Subbu the number two, Spender the English poet, and the office boy a frustrated would-be poet.

stem.en: Which statement about "Poets and Pancakes" is NOT correct?

options.en: Pancake was the name of a popular snack at the studio
The author worked at Gemini Studios
The MRA staged plays in Madras
The staff could not follow the English poet

explanation.en: Pancake was a brand of make-up, not a snack.

stem.en: Why did Gemini Studios' staff, though Gandhian in dress, support visitors like the MRA?

options.en: They wanted to leave films for politics
They hoped to act in the MRA plays
They shared the visitors' opposition to communism

explanation.en: The studio's anti-communist outlook matched the MRA's; khadi was dress, not a political programme.
